relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-security
relations.evidence: Specifies whether the Couchbase Web Console can be accessible over http. To disable access set this option to "1". To enable access set this option to "0".

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-security
relations.evidence: Specifies the cluster encryption level. The level is used when cluster encryption is turned on.

relations.subject: tls:cluster-encryption-level
relations.evidence: If your goal is to disable non-local http access completely, you should use the `--cluster-encryption-level`flag and set its value to "strict".

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-security
relations.evidence: Before setting the level to "strict" you will need to perform a number of important actions, see [Enforcing TLS](https://docs.couchbase.com/server/current/manage/manage-security/manage-tls.html#enforcing-tls).

notable_absence.finding: This page manages cluster-wide security policy (HTTP/HTTPS access, cluster encryption level, TLS minimum version, cipher suites, HSTS headers) yet cites no role:/privilege: concept at all - only the generic shared 'unauthorized error' boilerplate. Given the registry's 8.0 role split introduced role:security-admin specifically to hold 'security-administration privileges' including encryption configuration, the absence of any reference to that role (or its read-only counterpart role:ro-security-admin) on the CLI's own security-settings command is a striking gap for exactly the security-settings batch this round singled out as most likely to show RBAC drift.

cross_component_finding: The SYNOPSIS contains a literal typo: `[---cipher-suites <ciphers>]` uses a TRIPLE dash, where every other flag in the same SYNOPSIS line (and the OPTIONS section's own `--cipher-suites <cipher>`) uses a standard double dash. A reader copy-pasting from the SYNOPSIS block would pass an invalid argument to the shell. This is a small, purely mechanical error of exactly the kind expected from unreviewed, generated-looking SYNOPSIS blocks - and it sits in the same SYNOPSIS line as `[--hsts-max-age <seconds]`, which is missing its closing angle bracket ('<seconds' rather than '<seconds>'), a second bracket-matching slip in the same line.
cross_product_finding: n/a - no Capella/Mobile/SDK content; cluster-wide TLS/HTTP security settings via couchbase-cli are Server-only, with Capella exposing no equivalent CLI surface for these settings per this batch's evidence.
